originalTitle: US stocks today: Nasdaq, S&P fall over 1%, end lower for week as chip selloff broadens
simplifiedContent: The US stock market had a bad day, with two important groups of stocks, the Nasdaq and S&P, falling by more than 1%. This happened because companies that make computer chips, which are important for artificial intelligence, saw their stock prices drop sharply. This made investors nervous and caused them to sell other stocks as well. Even though some companies, like banks, reported good earnings, other companies like Netflix made gloomy predictions, which also hurt investor confidence. As a result, the stock market ended the week on a low note.

originalTitle: Reliance Retail Q1 revenue rises, but profit falls as e-commerce weighs
simplifiedContent: Reliance Retail, a big retail company, just released its financial results for the first quarter. Its revenue, or the total amount of money it made, went up by 8.2% compared to the same time last year. However, its profit, or the amount of money it made after expenses, actually decreased by 14.2% because the company spent a lot on its online shopping business. This decrease in profit is important because it shows that the company's investments in e-commerce are affecting its bottom line. The company's consumer business did well, with revenue more than doubling due to strong sales in areas like groceries and electronics.

originalTitle: JSW Steel’s profit doubles on revenue growth, beats estimates
simplifiedContent: JSW Steel, a steel company, made a profit of Rs 4,696 crore in the quarter ending June, which is more than double what they made last year. This happened because their revenue (the money they made from selling steel) increased by about 10%, and they also saved money on finance costs. Their total expenses only rose by less than 4%, which helped increase their earnings. This means the company performed better than expected, which is good news for investors. The company still plans to spend the same amount on new projects and investments as they had previously planned.

originalTitle: Netflix shares tumble 13% after weak sales forecast, hit 22-month low
simplifiedContent: Netflix's stock price dropped by 12.6% to its lowest point in 22 months. This happened because the company said it doesn't expect to make as much money as people thought it would, even though its recent financial results were okay. The company's growth is slowing down, which means it's not making as much money as it used to. This matters because it affects the value of Netflix's stock, which has been decreasing since mid-2025. As a result, investors are less confident in the company's future performance, which is why the stock price is falling.

originalTitle: Sebi clears automatic SWP, STP mandates for demat mutual fund holdings
simplifiedContent: The stock market regulator, Sebi, has made a new rule that affects how people invest in mutual funds. Previously, investors could only set up automatic instructions for mutual fund units that were held in a special account statement. Now, Sebi is allowing investors to set up automatic instructions for mutual fund units held in a demat account, which is a type of account that holds investments electronically. This means investors can now automatically transfer or withdraw money from their mutual fund investments held in a demat account. This change makes it easier for investors to manage their mutual fund investments.

originalTitle: Pulse of the Street: Earnings sentiment rescues volatile week; real test ahead
simplifiedContent: The Indian stock market had a good week, with two important indexes, the Sensex and Nifty, going up in value. The Sensex rose by 0.75% and the Nifty by 0.53% for the week, with most of the increase happening on Friday. On Friday, the Nifty jumped up by 1.1% and the Sensex by 1.25%, which is a big increase. This means that people who invested in the stock market made some money, at least for now. The Sensex also reached its highest closing level since June 12, 2026, which is a good sign for investors.
